---
title: "Missing data"
---

Suppose we want to compare the acoustic realization of American English /ɹ/ across speakers. For each production, we intend to record duration and several formant-frequency estimates. The signal is present, but the formant-tracking procedure does not yield a usable third-formant estimate for some tokens. What, exactly, is missing?

The missing value is not the speech token, and it is not the phonological category /ɹ/. It is one particular acoustic estimate for one recorded token. This distinction matters because a formant value is an analysis of the signal: a Praat [`Formant` object](https://fon.hum.uva.nl/praat/manual/Formant.html), for instance, stores estimated center frequencies and bandwidths frame by frame. An absent estimate thus records measurement failure, not an observed value of zero and not direct evidence that the speaker produced no third formant.

The separation between the linguistic unit, the intended measurement, and the recorded value is the **missing-data specification**. Before choosing a statistical method, we should be able to name all three.

## What counts as missing?

Several superficially similar blanks have different meanings.

- **An absent record:** a speaker who was never recruited or a corpus token that was never sampled has no row. This is a sampling or coverage problem, not a missing cell in the realized table.
- **Planned missingness:** a counterbalanced experiment may deliberately leave some participant--item combinations unpresented. Those omissions belong to the [design](../experimental-design/counterbalancing.qmd); they are not accidental nonresponses.
- **An undefined measure:** a word skipped on first pass has an observed skipping outcome, but no first-pass fixation duration. Reading studies consequently analyze skipping and fixation-contingent durations as distinct measures ([Rayner et al. 2011](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3543826/)). Coding the duration as `NA` does not create an unseen fixation duration.
- **Measurement, annotation, or tracking failure:** the recording exists, but a value that the protocol intended to recover is unavailable. A lost eye-tracker segment, an unresolved annotation, and a failed formant track belong here, though their causes differ.
- **Dropout:** a participant begins a longitudinal or multi-session study but supplies no later records. This is unit-level loss over time, not merely an empty acoustic cell.

These cases may all produce blanks after data are reshaped into a rectangle. But they imply different target populations, different observation processes, and different possible remedies. Imputation is relevant only after we have identified a value that was intended to be observed and is now unavailable.

## From locations to assumptions

We proceed in two steps. First, [missingness patterns](missingness-patterns.qmd) represent which intended values are observed. The indicator describes locations; it does not explain them. Second, [missingness mechanisms](missingness-mechanisms.qmd) state how the probability of observation may depend on named observed and unobserved variables. The labels MCAR, MAR, and MNAR are incomplete unless those variables and the unit of analysis are specified.

This distinction parallels the separation between a sampling design and an outcome model. The pattern is observed data. The mechanism is an assumption about the process that produced that pattern.

## Deletion, reconstruction, and checking

[Complete-case analysis](complete-case-analysis.qmd) retains rows observed on every variable required by a particular analysis. It thus defines a selection indicator. If selection depends on the response or a predictor, the retained rows may describe a different population from the eligible rows.

[Iterative PCA imputation](pca-imputation.qmd) takes a different route. It uses the [rank-$K$ reconstruction](../factorization/reconstruction.qmd) of a completed matrix to update its missing cells while returning observed cells to their measured values. The resulting number is a model-based prediction under a low-rank assumption. It is not a recovered observation, and a single completed matrix does not propagate uncertainty about the prediction.

Finally, [validation by artificial masking](validating-imputation.qmd) hides some observed values, fits the full procedure without them, and compares the held-out reconstructions with their known values. This extends the earlier distinction between [training and test data](../model-criticism-and-prediction/training-and-test-data.qmd) to matrix cells. It can reveal reconstruction failures under the tested masks, but it cannot reveal the values that were naturally missing.

The order of the module follows the decisions an analysis requires: (i) specify what should have been observed, (ii) describe where it is absent, (iii) state assumptions about why, (iv) make deletion explicit, (v) define one reconstruction method, and (vi) test that method under plausible artificial omissions. The upshot is simple. A blank becomes statistically interpretable only after we name its unit, variable, and observation process.
